title: Mitigate billing duplication from webhook retry storms causing proration drift
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: A transient retry storm from our webhook ingestion fleet produced repeated usage events for a subset of customers over a 4-hour window. Those duplicate usage rows were not deduplicated before the Stripe/NetSuite export job, causing duplicate invoice lines and incorrect proration for mid-cycle plan changes. This ticket contains the remediation plan: short-term mitigation, permanent ingestion deduplication, export hardening, and a reconciliation job to correct affected invoices.

Observed behavior: Duplicate usage rows (same customer, meter, interval, and identical payload) were inserted multiple times by the webhook processor during Kafka consumer retries when the downstream metering write acknowledged late. The downstream billing export treats usage rows as additive, so duplicates inflated token counts and produced duplicated invoice line items after export mapping. Proration calculations then skewed when plan switches happened during the affected window.

Root cause: Lack of strong idempotency/dedup key at the ingestion boundary and a blind export job that lacked an idempotency checkpoint/watermark. The retry loop semantics allowed reprocessing without a unique event identifier persisted on the usage document. Exacerbated by an ERLANG consumer restart pattern that redelivered an entire partition without per-message dedupe.

Scope: ~1,200 customers touched, ~2.4M duplicated token units across multiple plans, several dozen Stripe invoices with duplicated line items identified so far. Potential revenue misstatements and increased refunds/support cases.

Goals: 1) Stop ongoing duplication within 24 hours; 2) Prevent recurrence via ingestion and export guarantees; 3) Repair affected exported lines / NetSuite reconciliation; 4) Add observability and tests so this event is quickly detected and auto-mitigated in future.
acceptance_criteria: Webhook ingestion persists an idempotency key for every incoming usage event (customer_id + meter_id + event_uuid) and uses it to deduplicate writes.
Export job (Stripe/NetSuite) checkpoints by export_run_id and last_processed_event_id, and will not re-export identical usage rows; export is idempotent within a run.
Reconciliation job identifies and marks duplicated invoice lines in the export staging area and emits a corrective export to Stripe (credit/refund) and NetSuite adjustments for affected customers.
End-to-end integration tests simulate consumer restart and retry storms and assert no double-counting in the final export output.
Dashboards and alerting show duplicate-usage-rate metric with threshold alerting and an automated mitigation playbook linked.
Post-mortem published with root cause and follow-ups and customer communications template prepared for CS.
No further duplicates observed in production for 7 days post-deploy for the affected partitions.
implementation_notes: Add event_uuid field at the webhook edge (if missing) and normalize incoming ids in the ingestion lambda. For older events without event_uuid generate stable hash of payload fields but tag as heuristically-deduped.
Persist idempotency records in the usage write path using a compact bloom-backed side-table to keep latency low; fall back to full dedupe scan for borderline cases.
Modify export worker to include last_seen_event_id watermark per-customer-per-meter and write an export_run manifest to S3 with checksums to ensure idempotency across retries.
Introduce a fast reconciliation query in billing DB to find identical (customer,meter,interval,start_ts,units) rows where count > 1 and produce candidate correction actions.
When producing corrective exports for Stripe/NetSuite: tag with original_export_run_id, include human-readable audit_reason, and attach the dedupe manifest for accounting team review.
rollout_plan: Canary deploy changes to ingestion and export in us-west-2 for 2 hours with synthetic load that recreates the retry pattern. Monitor duplicate-usage-rate and export manifest checksums. If stable, expand to all regions over 2 hours. Full deploy gating requires reconciliation job to be runnable in dry-run mode and smoke tests green.
rollback_plan: If duplication increases or export manifests mismatch: immediately disable new ingestion idempotency flag (reads will still work), pause export workers, and revert ingestion consumer to previous image. Run emergency reconciliation to re-stabilize export staging area and notify ops and finance.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store (collision, expiry, perf).
Integration test harness that simulates Kafka consumer restart and massive redelivery; assert that final usage table dedupe rate is 0%.
E2E export test that creates a synthetic customer, writes duplicate usage events, runs export job, and validates Stripe export payload has no duplicated line items.
Backfill dry-run: run the reconciler in dry-run against the affected window and validate generated correction CSV matches manual audit.

2026-03-11 — Jonah M: Spiked a fix for dedupe at ingestion edge; prototype uses an append-only idempotency table keyed by event_uuid. Observed negligible latency impact in local load tests. Pending design review.
2026-03-12 — Priya Desai (Finance): Provided list of 42 invoices that already prompted support cases; requested priority for export reconciliation. Added as stakeholders.
2026-03-12 — Ops: Temporarily increased webhook consumer parallelism and surfaced duplicate-usage-rate metric on ops dashboard; confirmed spike ended after consumer restart window closed.
2026-03-13 — Jonah M: PR #903 opened for ingestion dedupe; running canary in us-west-2. Early telemetry shows duplicated-row-count down 99% for canary partitions.

2026-03-14 — Aisha K: Reconciler dry-run produced 5,200 candidate duplicate groups across the window. Working with Finance to approve corrective export schema. Next: schedule live corrective export after approvals.
